provisioning_notes: This is a design catalogue only: native_active is false, native_ids_admitted is false on every candidate, and no recipe, item, spell, effect, stat bundle, or client template is asserted to exist.

Field designs are ordinary useful combat-stat replacements intended for repeatable city batches. Their base leather forms stand alone; optional support or mail collaborators are separate child commissions and cannot become a mandatory cross-profession bottleneck for routine provisioning. No field entry requires a custom proc, recovery, fatigue, camp, supply, stealth, or fumble subsystem.

Masterworks take longer and consume scarcer real materials than field batches. Legendary commissions are funded, sequential five-stage work with preparation, forging or weaving, tempering, signature finishing, and inspection/attunement; proposed hours remain unratified.

Leatherworking owns armor forms in this catalogue. Weapons are deliberately excluded and must be commissioned from a separately qualified profession; a paired armor kit never silently creates a weapon route.

An artisan must have the actual skill, learned recipe, level, armor/form eligibility, station, materials, and customer fit for any later native admission. A blueprint or maker mastery record cannot teach a missing native recipe.

Boss themes shape form, stat emphasis, and signature vocabulary. Earned maker mastery is a separate uncapped personal record; it does not bypass per-item role/tier budgets or retroactively alter older gear.

Numbers, triggers, cooldowns, durations, ranges, proc rates, material quantities, native IDs, and property bundles are PROPOSED/unratified wherever mentioned. Exact behavior needs a native/client admission pilot and observed save/load/equip/mail lifecycle.

Real ingredient sourcing means a credited gatherer, guild stock, or purchased supply must reserve and reconcile actual hides, cord, thread, scales, resin, or cores. A planned order, mail handoff, or duplicate stack is not proof of a completed craft.

Priority follows the city-crafter direction: chest/legs/head/shoulders first, then bracers/feet/waist/gloves. The 18 designs deliberately cover those slots while giving physical, healer, caster, defensive, and expedition roles concrete ordinary gear. Field entries are future blueprints; immediate native-equivalent item, recipe, armor-form, and property mapping remains unqualified.
